key_insight: Vine Codes are a new class of qLDPC codes that achieve lower qubit overhead than surface codes while remaining compatible with nearest-neighbour gates on a planar square superconducting grid.
engineering_relevance: They offer a practical path to reduce hardware footprint in fault-tolerant quantum computing without requiring long-range couplers, which is attractive for superconducting architectures.
method: Generalised directional qLDPC construction to open-boundary planar grids using routing qubits.
Searched numerically for candidate codes and verified circuit distances.
Evaluated performance under circuit-level noise with native iSWAP and CZ operations.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports candidate codes such as [[121,4,6]], [[221,6,7]], and [[234,9,6]], with up to ~28% fewer data/measure qubits at circuit distance 7 and ~18% fewer total qubits at distance 10, plus better-than-surface-code performance at a near-term noise rate of 10^-3.
watch_item: The design still relies on routing qubits and custom open-boundary layouts, so practical advantage will depend on routing overhead, calibration complexity, and how well the assumed noise model matches real hardware.
paper_title: Vine Codes: Low-Overhead Quantum LDPC Codes on a Planar Square Grid
